name: MonarchLoadMore
title: LoadMore
summary: The footer of a paginated list: a Load more button with loading, failure and retry, the end of the list, a count and polite announcements.
whenToUse: As the last item of a LazyColumn whose data comes in pages from a cursor or an offset: tickets, activity, search results.
whenNotToUse: For a list that fits in one response, show it whole. For numbered pages people jump between, use a pager with page numbers.
api: @Composable fun MonarchLoadMore(hasMore: Boolean, onLoadMore: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, loading: Boolean = false, failed: Boolean = false, autoLoad: Boolean = false, showEnd: Boolean = true, loadedCount: Int? = null, totalCount: Int? = null, showCount: Boolean? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchLoadMoreLabels = MonarchLoadMoreLabels())

class MonarchLoadMoreLabels(loadMore: String? = null, loading: String? = null, failed: String? = null, retry: String? = null, end: String? = null, count: ((loaded: Int, total: Int?) -> String)? = null, loaded: ((added: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: hasMore
options.description: Whether there is another page. false shows the end line.

options.name: onLoadMore
options.description: Loads the next page. Not called while loading.

options.name: loading
options.description: A page is being fetched; the button shows progress and ignores taps.

options.name: failed
options.description: The last fetch failed; the failure is shown, the button becomes Retry and auto-loading pauses.

options.name: autoLoad
options.description: Loads the next page when the footer is composed, which in a lazy list means when it scrolls into view. The button stays.

options.name: showEnd
options.description: Shows and announces "That's everything" at the end.

options.name: loadedCount
options.description: The items on screen. Shown in the count; an increase is announced.

options.name: totalCount
options.description: The total, when the server knows it.

options.name: showCount
options.description: Shows the count. null shows it when loadedCount is given.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Called by Retry. null calls onLoadMore.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the strings and plurals monarch_loadmore_*, including the count and the announcement.

states.name: idle
states.description: The count and a small Load more button.

states.name: loading
states.description: The button shows progress, ignores taps and has the state "Loading".

states.name: failed
states.description: "Couldn't load more." in danger text and a Retry button.

states.name: end
states.description: "That's everything" in muted text, or nothing with showEnd = false.

appearance: A centered column with vertical padding: the count and the end line in muted caption text, the failure in the strong danger color, and a small secondary MonarchButton. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web also ships a useLoadMore hook that keeps the cursor and the pages; on Android the app's view model keeps them (or Paging's LazyPagingItems) and the footer only shows where loading stands. Auto-loading starts when the footer is composed instead of an IntersectionObserver, so there is no root margin: put the footer in the lazy list, where it is composed when it nears the screen. The web noun option is replaced by plurals in strings_loadmore.xml and the count and loaded labels. The web moves focus to the end line when the button disappears; Android leaves TalkBack focus to the system, and the end is announced. The failure is a line of text above the button instead of a MonarchInlineErrorRetry, so the one button keeps its place for Load more and Retry. iOS shares the name and the options.
accessibility: The button is a MonarchButton with a 48dp touch target; while loading it ignores taps and has the state "Loading".
A growing loadedCount is announced through a polite live region: "20 more items loaded."
A new failure and the end of the list are announced through the same live region; nothing is announced on the first composition.
The failure and the end are written as text, not only coloured.
Long messages wrap at the largest font size.
edgeCases: With autoLoad outside a lazy list every page loads at once, because the footer is always composed.
Auto-loading stays paused while failed is true; Retry or clearing failed resumes it.
A count that goes down, for example after a reset, is not announced.
